title: A randomized controlled trial to examine the effect of acupuncture strategies on pain relief and gastrointestinal recovery after bariatric surgery
summary:
Our preliminary work suggests that acupuncture may have a beneficial effect on pain relief and on the restoration of gastrointestinal function after bariatric surgery. This result is now to be examined in a randomized, placebo-controlled study in order to examine the effect of acupuncture on the postoperative recovery process. In addition, a triple blinded study design is used. This means that the investigators, the participating patients and also the persons responsible for monitoring, data management and the evaluation of the study are not informed about the individual treatment.  This is made possible by marking the acupuncture points and placebo points in different colors. This way of conducting the study guarantees that the results of the study are as objective and trustworthy as possible and are not dependent on the influence of individual people. 
5 min, 1 h and 24 h after the acupuncture the patient is examined regarding the complaints, the pain threshold as well as the temperature on the abdominal skin. A standard care group without intervention (acupuncture) is included.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Patients who undergo primary bariatric surgery for obesity
- Locus dolendi with maximum tenderness at points G1 to G6, VAS ≥ 3 (rest pain or when moving) - Minimum age of 18 years
- Sufficient communication skills
Exclusion criteria:
- Previous acupuncture experience for the same indication
- Missing body parts for acupuncture (e.g. extremities) or infection or malignant tumor at the site of needle placement
- Needle phobia
- Relevant mental disorders (e.g. borderline patients with a risk of self-harm)
- Serious coagulation disorders (e.g.: clinically relevant hemophilia)
